review_input.meaning: Addresses request to refresh bundled-runtime security evidence after 43.8.4 publication. Historical 27 October evidence is preserved.

decision.scope: Smallest current supported same-major stable update; no production dependency, host CI/toolchain or codec work.
decision.reason: Electron 43.8.4 is the latest supported same-major stable patch and carries the bundled Node security update. However, selected Chromium source retains the pattern addressed by Critical CVE-2026-118306. Its Windows source is built and no active Electron patch supplies the fix. Practical Bug Pocket exploitability was not demonstrated; current security approval and release acceptance remain held.
decision.broader_requirement: A runtime that contains the required Chromium fix, or specific equivalent-fix/non-applicability evidence, is needed before security approval. No newer 43.x stable is currently available. Do not silently migrate majors or build a custom cherry-picked runtime; report the compatibility/scope requirement first.

identity.artifact_notes: Official metadata only in this research. Root separately hashes downloaded/installed/packaged artifacts. Alternate FFmpeg is coordination evidence for EXA-65, not codec validation.

per_cve.disposition: Node 24.22.1 includes DNS input validation; main-process BYOK, feedback and Supabase paths use networking. No claim that app allowlists eliminate dependency-level resolution paths.
Fixed Node 24.22.1 TLS JavaScript verification. Native fetch/network paths exist; no Windows or app-input waiver is required.
Fixed Node 24.22.1 TLS verification. Resolver-specific exploit details do not justify declaring Windows safe without the fix.
Fixed decoder source verified independently of Node version: Electron links Chromium Brotli, whose selected150 source returns FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH and propagates status.
Fixed Node 24.22.1 HTTP Agent guard. Application/library HTTP client reachability was not excluded.
Fixed Node 24.22.1; retain conservative High because release notes group the TLS pair as High although advisory rates this CVE Medium.
Fixed Node 24.22.1. App packaging uses electron-builder ASAR; no user-land Node snapshot/SEA configuration found in package/scripts. This observation is not a general Electron snapshot waiver.
Fixed Node 24.22.1. App/scripts do not enable Node --permission; renderer sandboxing is a distinct boundary.

other_line_exclusions.disposition: Official advisory limits ZipFile finding to Node 26.x; selected embedded Node 24.x is outside affected line.
Official advisory limits wildcard Permission Model finding to Node 26.x; selected embedded Node 24.x is outside affected line.

brotli_source_proof.build_evidence: Node deps/brotli is removed from GN deps; Chromium //third_party/brotli:dec and :enc are linked instead.
brotli_source_proof.evidence: DecodeBlockTypeAndLength returns BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH when max_block_type <= 1; BROTLI_SAFE_WITH_STATUS propagates permanent errors for literal, command and distance switches.
brotli_source_proof.disposition: Specific fixed source/build path verified; older1.2.0 version string is not treated as vulnerable or safe by itself.

openssl_boringssl.evidence: node_openssl_path points to //third_party/boringssl, with explicit source comment replacing bundled OpenSSL.
openssl_boringssl.disposition: Do not claimNode release OpenSSL 3.5.9 update is shipped; Electron uses Chromium BoringSSL. Node JavaScript TLS hostname fixes still apply. This is not a blanket BoringSSL vulnerability-free claim.
openssl_boringssl.additional_limit: Electron also links Chromium V8 rather than Node bundled V8. Do not infer that every upstream Node third-party dependency update is shipped merely because the Node version reports 24.22.1.

desktop156_oct20_additional_comparison.scope: Additional source comparison only. Unmatched entries have not been classified as applicable, fixed, or excluded. Full working mapping preserved outsideGit as raw research; no blanket all-clear.

confirmed_source_fix_gap.evidence: Selected DatabaseCheckHelper::ScanDatabase calls RemoveFileInfo while the LevelDB iterator remains live. Official M150 fix scopes/destroys the iterator before removal. The source is in unconditional storage/browser sources; all 240 active Electron Chromium cherry-pick patches were checked and none touches this file/function. Independent focused review confirmed the comparison.
confirmed_source_fix_gap.application_limit: This demonstrates a shipped Windows source-level fix gap, not a reproduced Bug Pocket exploit. App-triggering and end-to-end exploitability remain untested; local-renderer CSP alone is not a sufficient exclusion.

limits: Confirmed source-level Critical fix gap prevents blanket security approval.
The remaining 48 current desktop entries are unresolved applicability/backport evidence, not demonstrated affected Bug Pocket vulnerabilities.
Three current desktop CVEs are excluded by explicit Android implementation/build evidence.
No newer-major-only exclusion is asserted without introduction evidence.
Earlier Chrome 156 and LTS comparisons are bounded source evidence, not a claim that all Chromium vulnerabilities are enumerated or fixed.
Passing component, full-test and unpacked smoke checks do not establish security approval, interactive acceptance or installed-package behavior.

observations.observation: Feedback default transport uses global fetch.

application_evidence.negative_search_limit: No direct dns.resolve/node:zlib Brotli/Permission Model/snapshot flags found in app source/scripts is only an observation; dependency reachability is not excluded.
